plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage clarifications, and an Excluded Claims definition covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, and IP infringement. Check the cap size against playbook thresholds and confirm payment obligations are outside the cap (21.3). Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability.

Vendor IP indemnity in 20.1 and conduct indemnities in 20.2; Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is narrow with carve-outs. Procedure in 20.4 and infringement remedies in 20.5 (cross-referenced by 9.3). Verify indemnities sit outside the liability cap via Excluded Claims in 21.3.

Section 12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to develop, buy, build, and engage other suppliers and disclaims non-compete commitments — beneficial to us. Confirm no contrary restriction elsewhere (note the exclusivity clause at 2.2 is handled under EXCLUSIVITY).

Section 2.2 (first of two clauses numbered 2.2) makes Vendor the sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the term — a direct breach of the no-exclusivity position, and it conflicts with 2.1 and 12.3. Primary redline target.

Section 7.2 (first clause numbered 7.2) obliges Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than those offered any other technology supplier — an MFN running against us, contrary to 12.3. Wrong-direction deviation; the invoicing clause at sec-7.2-2 is unrelated.

Section 12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, extends to 'engage' as well as solicit, and lacks a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out; compare the general-recruitment carve-out language in 12.3. Check duration and scope against the narrow, time-limited fallback.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency, and specific-trigger termination rights (9.1–9.3, 9.5); no general termination for convenience by Customer appears, and 8.1/8.2 lock a three-year term with 12-month renewals. Confirm across Sections 8–10 and 27.3 before treating as missing.

Section 8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months on a 180-day non-renewal notice — test the notice window against the playbook maximum. Uplift is capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent with 90 days' notice in 8.3, which likely satisfies the pricing limb.
New York law with New York County courts and no foreign arbitration (28.1–28.2), plus a pre-suit executive escalation in 28.3 that preserves urgent relief. Appears within accepted jurisdictions.

Customer may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent (24.1), Vendor is restricted (24.2), and Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination or repricing right (24.4). Licence transfer right in 13.3 cross-references Section 24.

Customer owns Customer Data and pre-existing IP (14.1) and Deliverables are assigned on creation subject to payment (14.2); Vendor Technology retained with a perpetual licence back via 13.2/14.3. Check the definitions (1.3, 1.4, 1.8) and the no-model-training restriction in 15.1 for any leakage of our IP or data to Vendor.

Section 13.1 extends access to Affiliates, contractors, and Authorized Users; 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured breach after notice and cure. Restrictions in 13.4 look standard.

Section 22.1 allows Vendor to audit Customer at any time without notice and to remotely access Customer systems — no notice, no frequency limit, on-site/system access; conflicts with 22.2's own prohibition on direct system access. Primary redline; 22.2 (cost allocation, 5% threshold) and 22.3 (confidentiality of findings) are supportive.

Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages on Customer for any dependency delay — liquidated damages running against us, uncapped in practice. Wrong-direction deviation; check interaction with the Section 21 cap.

Services performance warranty (19.1), 90-day Deliverable conformance plus term-long hosted conformance (19.2), malicious code and compliance warranties (19.3), and a repair/re-perform remedy with refund and non-exclusivity (19.4). Check the 90-day duration and remedy against the playbook minimum; disclaimer in 19.5 preserves express warranties.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M, and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers certificates, primacy, cancellation notice, and non-limitation of liability. Compare limits to playbook minimums.

Section 2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms non-ordering is not a breach; 7.1 bars unlisted minimum-use charges and 12.3 disclaims minimum-volume commitments. Favourable to us.

Section 11.1 gives up to six months' transition assistance at expiring rates, 11.2 requires data return within thirty days in machine-readable form with no fee-dispute hostage, and 11.3 covers certified deletion; 10.2 adds Deliverable delivery and refunds.
